# Results — Study 472 (WaveTrend, LazyBear)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a WT1
cross up through its signal line WT2 while oversold (below ~−60) is a high-probability buy** —
encoded as a mechanical rule. WaveTrend lines are causal EMAs/SMA of the typical price
(HLC3); the cross is read on the close of *t*, the long is entered at the **next close** (one
documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Indicator | WaveTrend (LazyBear): n1 (channel EMA) = 10, n2 (average EMA) = 21, signal SMA = 4, oversold band = −60 |
| Entries | **115** mechanical oversold cross-ups pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Timing / costs | causal lines (no look-ahead); cross read on close of *t*, enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument timing study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — WaveTrend cross-up vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch cross-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = cross − random (random seed = 7).

| horizon | n | cross-up | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 115 | +97.7 bps  | 61% | +3.37 | −19.2 bps | **+116.9 bps** | +95.7 bps  | +2.83 | 0.005 |
| 10-day | 115 | +176.8 bps | 70% | +4.70 | −1.1 bps  | **+177.9 bps** | +174.8 bps | +3.45 | 0.001 |
| 20-day | 115 | +255.4 bps | 68% | +4.73 | +22.0 bps | **+233.4 bps** | +253.4 bps | +3.39 | 0.001 |
| 60-day | 110 | +458.1 bps | 65% | +3.27 | +57.3 bps | **+400.8 bps** | +456.1 bps | +3.02 | 0.003 |

The single-seed table above (random seed = 7) makes this look like a **rare positive**: the
cross-up appears to beat the drift baseline at the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar across all four horizons.
But the random-entry baseline is a *sample* of the drift, so a single seed can fluke a *t* > 2.
The honest test — the decisive one below — is the **seed-averaged** Welch *t*.

## The decisive test — seed-averaged Welch *t* over 30 baseline seeds (the honest bar)

A single lucky baseline seed is not an edge (Study 452 caught this exact trap: a seed=7 baseline
gave 20d Welch *t* = 3.08 but averaging over 20 seeds collapsed it to +1.73, correctly graded
None). So we sweep **30 baseline seeds** (1…30), recompute the cross-vs-random Welch *t* per
horizon, and report the **mean** and **spread**. The cross signal is held fixed; only the random
baseline is reseeded.

| horizon | seed-avg Welch *t* | min | max | % of seeds *t* ≥ 2 | survives robustly? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| 5-day  | **+1.97** | +0.50 | +3.23 | 50% | **NO** |
| 10-day | **+2.74** | +0.99 | +3.98 | 87% | **YES** |
| 20-day | **+2.37** | +0.95 | +3.72 | 70% | **YES (marginal)** |
| 60-day | **+1.29** | +0.10 | +3.02 | 17% | **NO** |

Averaged over seeds, the edge clears *t* ≥ 2 **only at 10–20 days** — and even at 20d, 30% of
seeds dip below 2. At 5 days (1.97) and 60 days (1.29) it **fails**. The single-seed=7 headline
(2.83 / 3.45 / 3.39 / 3.02) sat on the *lucky* side of these distributions; it over-stated the
breadth of the result. This is exactly the Study 452 pattern.

The **zero-sampling-noise unconditional drift baseline** (every bar's forward return — no seed)
agrees: the edge survives at *t* ≥ 2 only at 10d (+2.77, *p* = 0.007) and 20d (+2.56, *p* =
0.012), not at 5d (+1.89, *p* = 0.062) or 60d (+1.38, *p* = 0.172). Two independent honest
baselines point the same way.

So the signal is **real but faint, narrow, and seed-fragile** — concentrated at 10–20 days, thin
on trades (115 in 21.4 years, ~1 per ETF per year), and below the robust bar at the two outer
horizons. That is a **Weak** signal, not a Real one, and a **Fragile** tradability.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the cross-up beats random in 4 of 5 names

| ticker | entries | cross-up | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 20 | +345.7 bps | +2.86 | +35.0 bps | **+310.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 22 | +59.6 bps  | +0.42 | +62.0 bps | **−2.5 bps** |
| IWM | 27 | +270.1 bps | +2.17 | −28.5 bps | **+298.6 bps** |
| DIA | 22 | +427.1 bps | +3.23 | +34.7 bps | **+392.4 bps** |
| GLD | 24 | +185.6 bps | +2.61 | +6.6 bps  | **+179.0 bps** |

The cross-up beats random in **4 of 5** names (only QQQ is flat), and SPY/DIA/IWM/GLD all post
large positive deltas — a coherent cross-instrument signal, the opposite of the relabelled-drift
pattern. The per-ticker counts (20–27) are tiny, so individual *t*'s are noisy.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the wave, the edge collapses

The decisive "does the geometry matter?" test: keep WT1's marginal (its values, so the oversold
band still bites the same fraction of the time) but **permute its first differences** before
re-cumulating, destroying the wave structure that makes "cross up from oversold" meaningful.
Re-run the *exact* same rule on the scrambled line.

| test | observed cross-up 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY scrambled-signal WaveTrend | +345.7 bps | **0.011** | 500 |

Only **~1% of scrambled-wave signals match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.011, robust across
placebo seeds {1, 7, 42, 472, 2024} at *p* = 0.011–0.017). When the oscillator's wave structure
is destroyed, the SPY 20-day edge collapses — so *where the signal exists* the WaveTrend geometry
**is** load-bearing. Important caveat: this placebo probes only the single horizon/name where the
cross is strongest (SPY, 20d). It confirms the wave carries information **there**, but it cannot
rescue the 5- and 60-day horizons that fail the seed-averaged test above — which is why the
forecasting thesis is **Mixed**, not Confirmed.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness is honest (no false positive, banks a real bounce)

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* WaveTrend bounce (knob `edge`), the same cross-up rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the positive real-tape result is not a broken detector.

| planted edge | n | cross-up | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 33 | +114.8 bps | 61% | +1.25 |
| **0.60** (real planted bounce) | 24 | +549.4 bps | 88% | **+4.89** |

With no planted bounce the control sits below the *t* ≥ 2 bar (no false positive); a real planted
bounce lights up at *t* = +4.89 with an 88% win-rate. The detector is live and calibrated.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** On the **seed-averaged** Welch test (30 baseline seeds — the honest bar), the
  WaveTrend oversold cross-up beats a drift-matched random baseline at *t* ≥ 2 **only at 10–20
  days** (mean *t* = +2.74 / +2.37); at 5 days (+1.97) and 60 days (+1.29) it **fails**, and even
  at 20d only 70% of seeds clear 2. The single-seed=7 headline (+2.83 / +3.45 / +3.39 / +3.02) sat
  on the lucky side of the seed distribution and over-stated the result — exactly the Study 452
  trap. The zero-noise unconditional-drift baseline agrees (significant only at 10d/20d). So the
  signal is real but **faint and narrow** — Weak, not Real.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Only **115 trades** in 21 years (~1 per ETF per year); over 30 seeds
  the 20d Welch *t* spans +0.95 → +3.72 (only ~70% clear 2) and the edge lives in a thin 10–20-day
  band. Real but seed-fragile and thin — not bankable on this sample.
- **"Does the WT cross forecast?" — MIXED.** The scrambled-signal placebo (SPY, 20d) rejects the
  scrambled-wave null (*p* = 0.011), so *where the signal exists* the WaveTrend geometry carries
  real information — but the cross robustly beats random only in the 10–20-day window, so the broad
  folklore claim (a high-probability buy at *every* horizon) is **not** confirmed. The synthetic
  control confirms the harness fires only on a real bounce (so the 10–20d effect is genuine, not a
  broken pipeline).
